model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 40 to 65, with tick marks every 5 units. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% accuracy and increases slightly to about 44% as co-occurrence number increases. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at around 44% and rises to approximately 56%. The FT method (blue line with triangular markers) starts at about 40% and reaches roughly 47%. The MEMIT method (purple line with pentagonal markers) begins at approximately 44% and increases to about 54%. The IKE method (red line with triangular markers) starts at around 43% and rises to about 49%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) shows the highest accuracy, starting at about 51% and increasing steadily to approximately 66%. All lines show an upward trend, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the range of co-occurrence numbers.
